Getting started · Start

Overview

What the guide covers and the process from start to finish.

This guide describes how forms are created in the Exxat form builder. Two methods are covered: creating a new form, and duplicating a form that already exists in a university (tenant). The guide also introduces the editor that opens once a form has been created or replicated, including the default values of a new form. It then covers the Sections tab, where sections and fields are added, instance-based forms, the Layout tab, and the Workflow tab.

The top menu of the builder contains four areas: Forms, Multi Layout, Stakeholders and Templates. Form creation starts in the Forms area.

Process summary

  1. Open the landing page and choose whether to create a new form or start with an existing one.
  2. To create a new form, enter the Form Name and a unique Form name abbr (Feature ID), then select Create Form. The editor opens with default values already filled in (Step 6). Complete the remaining App Definition fields and keep autoReminder off.
  3. To duplicate a form, select the Tenant Id and OOU Code, tick Duplicate form, enter a new Target Form name abbr, and select List Forms.
  4. Choose the form to replicate from the Forms List.
  5. Review the replicated form in the editor, apply the version naming format to the form name, and save.

For a complete walkthrough of configuring an instance-based form, see Step 12.

Part 1 of 12 · Step 1

Landing page

The landing page presents two options side by side.

OptionContentsPurpose

Part 2 of 12 · Step 2

Create a new form

Use the Create A New Form panel on the left of the landing page.

  1. Form Name. Type or paste the name of the form, as specified in the requirement.
  2. Form name abbr (Feature ID). Enter a unique abbreviation. Its purpose is to keep each form separate from all other forms. Spaces are not permitted anywhere in it, including between its parts. The naming rules are set out in the next section.
  3. Create Form. Select the button once both fields are complete.
NoteThe Form name abbr is also known as the Feature ID. Two forms must not share the same Feature ID, so it should be treated as a unique identifier.

After Create Form is selected, the editor opens with several fields already filled in. These default values are described in Step 6.

Part 3 of 12 · Rules

Feature ID naming rules

Standard pattern

The Feature ID is built from three parts:

  1. The initials of the words in the form name.
  2. The university OU code.
  3. The domain.

Permitted characters

Permitted

Capital letters (A to Z), small letters (a to z), numbers (0 to 9) and the underscore ( _ ).

Not permitted

Spaces of any kind, including between the parts of the abbreviation, and all other special characters such as hyphens, dots, slashes, brackets, @, # and &.

Illustration

The following uses made-up values. For a form named "Student Health Immunization Form", with an OU code of 1234 and a domain of xyz, the parts may be joined with underscores as SHIF_1234_xyz. The same value written with spaces, SHIF 1234 xyz, is not valid. An underscore replaces any space.

Character check

Enter a Feature ID below to confirm that it contains only permitted characters. This check does not test uniqueness.

Part 4 of 12 · Step 3

Start with an existing form

Use the Start With An Existing Form panel on the right when a form already exists and needs to be duplicated or replicated, rather than built from the beginning.

  1. Tenant Id. Open the dropdown and select the university that the form belongs to.
  2. OOU Code. Select the OOU Code of the domain in which the form is located within the tenant.
  3. Duplicate form. Tick this checkbox to copy the form. The Target Form name abbr field then appears.
  4. Target Form name abbr. Enter a new Feature ID for the duplicated form. It must differ from the Feature ID of the original form.
  5. List Forms. Select the button to open the Forms List (Step 4).
ImportantThe Target Form name abbr must be a new Feature ID. It cannot conflict with the Feature ID of the older form. The naming rules in the previous section apply: initials of the form name, OU code and domain, using only letters, numbers and underscores, with no spaces. The form name of the new version follows a separate convention, described under Version naming for duplicated forms.
FieldEntryRemarks
Tenant IdThe university the source form belongs toSelected from the dropdown list
OOU CodeThe code of the domain the form is in, within that tenantMust belong to the selected tenant
Duplicate formCheckbox, ticked to copy the formReveals the Target Form name abbr field
Target Form name abbrA new Feature ID for the duplicated formMust differ from the original Feature ID
List FormsButtonOpens the Forms List

Part 5 of 12 · Rules

Version naming for duplicated forms

When a new version of an existing form is created, the form name must not be given a prefix or suffix such as "New". Instead, the version month and year are always appended to the end of the form name, in the following format:

<Form Name> Ver.MM.YYYY

ExampleStudent Evaluation of Preceptor Ver.08.2026

Format rules

  • Keep the original form name unchanged, followed by a single space.
  • Write Ver. with a capital V and a full stop.
  • MM is the month as two digits (for example 08 for August).
  • YYYY is the year as four digits (for example 2026).
  • Separate the month and the year with a full stop.
  • Do not add "New" or any other prefix or suffix to the form name.
Form nameStatusReason
Student Evaluation of Preceptor Ver.08.2026CorrectOriginal name followed by Ver.MM.YYYY
New Student Evaluation of PreceptorIncorrect"New" added as a prefix
Student Evaluation of Preceptor NewIncorrect"New" added as a suffix
Student Evaluation of Preceptor Ver.8.2026IncorrectThe month must be two digits (MM)
Student Evaluation of Preceptor Ver 08 2026IncorrectMissing full stops after Ver and between month and year

An existing form that follows this convention can be seen in Figure 6: "Student Evaluation of Clinical Site Ver.09.2026".

Version name builder

Enter the original form name and choose the month and year to generate the name for the new version.

Part 6 of 12 · Step 4

Choose a form from the Forms List

Selecting List Forms opens the Forms List window over the landing page. The form to be replicated is chosen here.

Window contents

  • A Search forms box at the top, for finding a form by name.
  • A numbered list of the forms available for the selected tenant and OOU Code.
  • An arrow at the end of each row, used to select that form.
  • A close (X) button in the top right corner, to leave without making a selection.

Selecting the form

  1. Locate the form. Scroll the list, or use Search forms.
  2. Verify the title. Read the full title carefully. Some forms have near-identical versions, for example the 12 Week and 16 Week versions of one evaluation tool.
  3. Select the form. Click the form in the list. It is then replicated.
Before selectingConfirm that the Tenant Id, OOU Code and Target Form name abbr are correct on the page behind the window. They determine the source of the copy and the Feature ID of the new form.

Choosing the Feature Type

The Feature Type dropdown offers three options.

OptionWhen it is used
CustomThe form that is generally created. This is the default.
MultipleResponseChosen when multiple responses will be submitted for the form. The steps are described in Step 14.
StandardAvailable in the dropdown. Its use is not covered in this guide.

Fields to complete in App Definition

The following App Definition fields are empty on a new form. They are completed according to the requirement.

FieldWhat to enter
Actor DetailsThe actors who will fill up the form.
Workflow DetailsThe workflow for the form, set according to the requirement: which actor fills the form, which actor signs or reviews it, and which actor has view access only.
Auto Notification DetailsThe notifications that are active in this particular form.

Summary: creating a simple new form

The Form tab, which is the first page of the editor, is all that needs to be completed to create a simple new form. The steps are:

  1. On the landing page, enter the Form Name and a unique Form name abbr (Feature ID), then select Create Form.
  2. On the Form tab, confirm the automatic values: Form Name, Form Name Abbreviation, Report Type (Custom), Feature Type (Custom), and Label, Short label, Name and Detail.
  3. Complete Actor Details, Workflow Details and Auto Notification Details according to the requirement.
  4. Select RawData in the App Definition Report Type dropdown.
  5. Select who will fill up the form first in Initiated By.
  6. Make sure autoReminder is off.
  7. Select Save at the top right.
NoteIf multiple responses will be submitted for the form, choose MultipleResponse in Feature Type instead. That process is described in Step 14.

Part 9 of 12 · Step 7

Sections (Layout Summary)

The Sections tab is where the questions of a form are organised. The area is called the Layout Summary. Its heading shows the identifier of the form followed by LayoutSummary, for example Evaluation.Test_abc_123.LayoutSummary. A section is created first, and fields (questions) are then added to it.

On first opening, the tab is empty except for the heading and a row of controls on the right: a Caption field (marked * as required) and an Add Section button, which is greyed out until a caption is entered.

Creating a section

  1. Open the Sections tab.
  2. Type the name of the section in the Caption field. The Add Section button becomes active.
  3. Click Add Section. The section is created.

The new section appears as a row showing its name, with the message "No Fields Added" beneath it. On the right of the row are an Add Field button and three icons, whose functions are not covered here.

Adding a field

Click Add Field on the section. A box appears with two sub-tabs, Main and Advanced. The Main sub-tab is described first.

ItemWhat it is
DescriptionThe question that needs to be added.
Meta InformationThe sub-information related to that particular question.
Tooltip message, Tooltip Position, Default value, PlaceholderFurther fields in the Content area. Not covered yet.
Control typeA required dropdown (marked *) that sets the kind of field. It starts as label. Control types are covered separately.
ValidationsUsed to make the question mandatory. Starts with "No Validations Added" and an Add Validation button.
Save and CancelButtons at the bottom of the box.

The Advanced sub-tab is described after the validation steps.

Choosing the control type

The Control type dropdown lists the kinds of field that can be used. The options visible in the screenshot are label, textbox, textarea, checkbox, radio, select, auto-fill and datepicker, followed by further options (the list scrolls). Each control type will be explained in a separate document.

Adding a validation

Validations decide whether a question is mandatory. If a question does not need to be mandatory, no validation needs to be added.

  1. Click Add Validation. A numbered row appears with a Name dropdown.
  2. In Name, choose required to make the question mandatory.
  3. A second dropdown, Message, appears. Choose the message that suits the question best.
  4. Select Save in the field box.

Choosing the message

The message is the text shown if the question is left unanswered. Pick the one that fits the kind of question. Based on the wording of each message:

MessageSuits
This field is required.A general question, such as a text answer
Please select the appropriate option.A question where one option is chosen
Please select the appropriate options.A question where more than one option can be chosen
Please select the date.A date question
This field requires a signature. Please sign here.A signature question
Please select the appropriate rating.A rating question
NoteWhile the Name or Message is still empty, the Save button stays greyed out and a red message appears, for example "validations[0].name is a required field". It clears once both are selected. The X beside a validation row removes that validation.

Summary: adding a section and a question

  1. Open the Sections tab (Layout Summary).
  2. Type the section name in Caption and click Add Section.
  3. Click Add Field on the section.
  4. On the Main sub-tab, enter the question in Description and any sub-information in Meta Information.
  5. Choose the Control type that suits the question.
  6. If the question must be answered, click Add Validation, choose required, and choose a suitable Message.
  7. Open the Advanced sub-tab and enter a unique Property Name for the question.
  8. Select Save.

Adding the first summary

ImportantAt first, add the first summary. It is the starting point for adding instance fields.

In the example, the summary row is named Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.Student, for the Student instance.

Adding the sections for an actor

Open the summary row by clicking its expand arrow. Its details appear, with three sub-tabs: Sections, Fields and FieldsInstances. The Sections sub-tab comes first.

ImportantAt first, add the sections that need to be editable or not editable on the actor's side. In this example the summary is for the Student actor.
  1. Expand the summary row and stay on the Sections sub-tab.
  2. Use the Select a section dropdown at the bottom of the list, with the plus button beside it, to add a section to the list.
  3. For each section, set the Edit checkbox: tick it if the section should be editable on the actor's side, and leave it unticked if it should not be.
  4. Click Update at the bottom to save the changes.

In Figure 26, the first section (the Instructions section) has Edit unticked, so it is not editable for the Student. The other eleven sections have Edit ticked, so they are editable.

Adding instances

Click Add Instances. An area appears where the instances are handled.

Selecting the properties

Open the Properties dropdown. It lists property names, each with a checkbox. Select the property names of the questions that need to be added as an instance.

  1. Click Add Instances.
  2. Open the Properties dropdown.
  3. Tick the property names of the questions that need to be added as an instance.
NoteThe entries in this list are property names such as Q1, Q2 and Q3. This is where the unique Property Name given to each question in Step 7 is used, which is why each Property Name must be unique.

Selecting the instances

Open the Select Instances dropdown. It lists the instances, each with a checkbox: Student and Instructor. Select only the instances that are needed at this step.

ImportantAt the Student step, add only the Student instance, so that only the Student is able to edit. Do not add the Instructor at this step.
  1. Open Select Instances.
  2. Tick only Student at the Student step.
  3. Click Add Instance.

Adding the questions, the instance and the caption

With the property names chosen and the Student instance selected, the questions are added and the instance is given a caption accordingly.

  1. In Properties, select the questions you want. In the example, Q1 to Q41 are selected. They appear as removable chips, and the block header lists them (Q1, Q2, Q3 and so on up to Q41).
  2. Add the instance using Select Instances and Add Instance. At the Student step only Student is added. The Instructor is not added.
  3. Enter the Caption for the instance accordingly.
  4. Keep Edit ticked, so that the Student is able to edit.
  5. Click Update.
Item in the instance rowShown in Figure 32
Instance IdStudent (row 1). Greyed out.
CaptionText for the instance. In the example it starts with a span tag that sets a colour (olive). The full text is cut off in the screenshot.
EditTicked, so the Student is able to edit.
XA button at the end of the row. Not covered yet.

Using separate instance blocks for different captions

When different groups of questions need different captions, create a separate instance block for each group. Click Add Instances again to create another block. Each block has its own properties, its own instance and its own caption.

BlockPropertiesWhy it is separate
1Q1 to Q41The text area questions, which use the Student and Instructor instances.
2D1C, d2C, D3C to D10CThe comment fields, which need a caption for Student comments or Instructor comments.
3A1 to A27The rating questions, which get their own instance and caption in the same way.

Each block shows its properties in its header when collapsed. The open block in Figure 33 shows the Student instance, a caption that starts with a span tag that sets a colour (olive), and the Edit checkbox unticked.

The block for the rating questions

The rating questions are handled the same way, in a block of their own. Click Add Instances once more, select the rating questions in Properties, add the instance, and enter the caption accordingly.

In Figure 34 the open block shows properties A1 to A27, the Student instance, a caption that starts with a span tag that sets a colour (olive), and the Edit checkbox ticked.

ImportantEach property name still has to be unique, and each property is selected in the block whose caption suits it.

Copying the first summary

Once the instance blocks of the first summary are created, the summary is complete. When all the blocks are collapsed, each block shows only its list of properties.

ImportantAfter the different instances are created, copy the first summary and edit the copy accordingly.

The second summary: Student Display

The copy is edited to become a second summary for the Student, in which the Student does not need to edit the form. In the list it appears as Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.Student-2, and its Summary Id is changed to Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.StudentDisplay.

In Figure 43 the heading reads Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.StudentDisplay. The first summary has an open eye icon and the second has a crossed-out eye icon. These are not covered yet.

The Instructor summary

The Instructor needs to fill the same questions, so the summary for the Instructor has Edit ticked on the sections. In the screenshots this summary is named Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.Faculty.

  1. On the Sections sub-tab, tick Edit on the sections the Instructor will fill.
  2. Go to the FieldsInstances sub-tab.
  3. In each instance block, add the Instructor as the actor: open Select Instances, tick Instructor, and click Add Instance.
  4. Tick Edit on the Instructor row, so that the Instructor is able to edit the form.
  5. Leave Edit unticked on the Student row, because the Student does not need to fill the form here.
  6. Click Update.
Row in the blockCaptionEditMeaning
1. StudentStarts with a span tag that sets the colour oliveUntickedThe Student does not fill the form in this summary.
2. InstructorStarts with a span tag that sets the colour maroonTickedThe Instructor is able to edit the form.

The fourth summary: Faculty Display

The last summary is Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.FacultyDisplay. At this stage no actor needs to edit, so Edit is unticked on the Sections sub-tab and on the FieldsInstances sub-tab. There is then no editing at this stage.

  1. On the Sections sub-tab, untick Edit for every section.
  2. On the FieldsInstances sub-tab, untick Edit on every instance row in every block.
  3. Click Update.

The fifth summary: Admin

The Admin summary is Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.Admin. The Admin is able to edit for both actors, so the Edit option is kept ticked for both the Student and the Instructor.

Part 11 of 12 · Step 10

Workflow tab

The Workflow tab is where the workflow of the form is set up. The layout prepared on the Layout tab (Step 9) is used to add the steps of the workflow.

The workflow for the example form is: the Student fills and submits the form, then the Instructor fills and submits the form.

The steps in the example form

Part 1 of 2 · Step 8

Instance-based forms

Some forms are configured as instance-based forms. In these forms, instances are added according to the actors who fill up the form.

Making the form instance-based

On the Form tab, the instanceForm checkbox sits beside the Form Name Abbreviation. It is unticked on a new form.

ImportantTick instanceForm when creating an instance-based form.

Instances on the Form tab

At the bottom of the Form tab, below the Help and Rules sub-tabs, an Instances list is shown. Each instance is a numbered row.

Item in each rowWhat it is
Instance IdA required entry (marked *) naming the instance. In the example: Student, and Instructor.
CaptionEmpty in the example. Not covered yet.
EditA checkbox, unticked in the example. Not covered yet.
XA button at the end of each row. Not covered yet.

One instance for each actor

ImportantAdd the instances according to the actors who will fill up the form. If two actors fill up the form, add two instances.

Part 2 of 2 · Step 13

How the form appears for multiple actors

This is how the instances for multiple actors appear on the finished form. Each question is shown once for every actor who fills it up, so the Student and the Instructor each get their own answer box for the same question. The actor label comes from the caption of the instance: the Student label is shown in olive and the Instructor label in maroon, matching the colours set in the captions (Step 9).

Questions

The section heading and its description appear first. The question text, entered as the Description in Step 7, is repeated above each actor's box. The required asterisk (*) follows the actor label.

Comments

Ratings

How the blocks relate to what is shown

Block in the Layout tabWhat the actors see
Q1 to Q41Student* (olive) and Instructor* (maroon) answer boxes under each question.
D1C to D10CStudent Comments (olive) and Instructor Comments (maroon) boxes. No asterisk is shown.
A1 to A27Student Rating* (olive) and Instructor Rating* (maroon) with the options P, W, NI and F.

This is why a separate instance block is created for each group of questions in Step 9: each group needs its own caption for the actor label.

Instance-based forms · Step 12

Step 12: Configuring an instance-based form, start to finish

The full configuration checklist, tab by tab.

This step brings the earlier steps together as one procedure for configuring an instance-based form, such as a form filled up by two actors, Student and Instructor. Each item points to the step that describes it in detail.

A. Form tab

  1. Create the form. On the landing page, enter the Form Name and a unique Form name abbr (Feature ID), then select Create Form (Step 2). The Feature ID uses only letters, numbers and underscores, with no spaces. Alternatively, duplicate an existing form (Steps 3 to 5).
  2. Check the defaults. Confirm that Report Type and Feature Type are Custom, and that Label, Short label, Name and Detail show the form name (Step 6).
  3. Tick instanceForm (Step 8).
  4. Complete the App Definition fields (Steps 6 and 11): Actor Details (Student, Instructor), Workflow Details (Student fills and submits the form, Instructor fills and submits the form), Auto Notification Details, Report Type (RawData) and Initiated By (who starts the form). Keep autoReminder off.
  5. Add the instances in the Instances list at the bottom of the Form tab, one for each actor who fills up the form: Student and Instructor (Steps 8 and 11).

B. Sections tab

  1. Add the sections. Type the section name in Caption and click Add Section (Step 7).
  2. Add the fields. In each section, click Add Field. Enter the question in Description and any sub-information in Meta Information, choose the Control type, add a required validation with a suitable message if the question must be answered, and give each question a unique Property Name on the Advanced sub-tab (Step 7).

C. Layout tab

  1. Add the first summary (Step 9), the Student summary, for example Summary.NRSE_360MN_TEF.Student.
  2. Add the sections to the summary on the Sections sub-tab, and tick Edit on the sections the actor edits (Step 9).
  3. Set up the FieldsInstances sub-tab. Click Add Instances, select the property names of the questions, select the instance with Select Instances, click Add Instance, and enter the caption. Create a separate block for each group that needs a different caption, such as the questions, the comments and the ratings. Tick Edit for the actor who edits (Step 9).
  4. Copy the first summary and edit each copy for the next stage (Step 9):
    • StudentDisplay: Edit unticked everywhere, so the Student does not edit.
    • Faculty: Edit ticked for the Instructor and unticked for the Student.
    • FacultyDisplay: Edit unticked everywhere, so no one edits.
    • Admin: Edit ticked for both the Student and the Instructor.

D. Workflow tab

  1. Add the workflow steps (Step 10). In the example the steps are Start, Save, FacultyReview, FacultySave and Complete. How each step is set up is not covered yet.

E. Save and publish

  1. Save. Select Save at the top right of the editor.
  2. Publish the form in the appropriate tenant.

To see how the finished form appears to the actors, see Step 13.

NoteThe screens for publishing the form in the tenant, and the Notification and Terms tabs, are not covered in this guide yet.

Multi response forms · Step 14

Step 14: Multi response forms

MultipleResponse, isMultiResponse and the first date field.

A multi response form is used when multiple responses will be submitted for the form. It is set up by choosing MultipleResponse as the Feature Type and ticking isMultiResponse. This part uses the example form Student Volunteer Record, with the Feature ID MSOT_SVR_PLNU, whose first field is Date of Initiation.

Steps at a glance

  1. In App Definition, select Feature Type, then MultipleResponse.
  2. Tick the isMultiResponse checkbox.
  3. Create a field at the top. In Description enter Date of Initiation, select the control type datepicker, and in Validations add required with the message Please select the date.
  4. Go to the Advanced sub-tab and enter the Property Name initiatedOn.
  5. Click Save.
  6. Save and publish the form in the particular tenant.
  7. Check the preview.

1. Select MultipleResponse as the Feature Type

On the Form tab, open the Feature Type dropdown in the App Definition group. It offers Custom, MultipleResponse and Standard. Select MultipleResponse.

In the example, the form name is Student Volunteer Record and the Form Name Abbreviation (Feature ID) is MSOT_SVR_PLNU. Label, Short label and Name show the form name.

2. Tick isMultiResponse

In the option checkboxes of App Definition, tick isMultiResponse. It is unticked by default.

3. Create the first field: Date of Initiation

Create a field at the top of the form (see Step 7 for adding sections and fields). On the Main sub-tab:

  • Description: Date of Initiation
  • Control type: datepicker

The Control type dropdown in this screenshot lists these options, and the list continues below them:

Control types visible in the list
label, textbox, textarea, checkbox, radio, select, auto-fill, datepicker, timepicker, file-upload, esign, slider, formula, selection-list

Validation

Click Add Validation. Set Name to required, and choose the message Please select the date. The date message suits a date question.

4. Enter the Property Name

Go to the Advanced sub-tab of the field and enter the Property Name initiatedOn. As with every question, the Property Name must be unique (Step 7).

5. Save, publish and check the preview

  1. Click Save.
  2. Save and publish the form in the particular tenant.
  3. Check the preview.

The preview shows how the Date of Initiation field is created.

What the preview showsIn the example
BannerA note that this is a sample of the evaluation form, not intended for entering and saving information. Anything entered will not be saved.
Who will be filling-up the form?Student
Workflow DetailsStudent fills and submits the form, faculty reviews the form.
Notification DetailsNo notifications are activated.
Date of InitiationShown with a red asterisk, because it is required, and a date field with the placeholder MM/DD/YYYY.
NoteThe screens for publishing the form in the tenant are not covered yet. The other content below the date field in the preview, such as the directions, purposes and requirements, is not covered in this part.

Reference · Reference

Glossary

Every term used in the Form Builder, in one list.

Tenant Id
A unique name for each university. When duplicating a form, the university the form belongs to is selected from this dropdown.
OOU Code
Indicates which domain the form is in. When duplicating, the OOU Code of the domain where the required form is located within the tenant is entered.
Form Name
The name of the form, typed or pasted as specified in the requirement.
Form name abbr (Feature ID)
A unique abbreviation that keeps each form separate from the others. It is built from the initials of the form name, the university OU code and the domain. Only capital letters, small letters, numbers and underscores are permitted, with no spaces.
Duplicate form
A checkbox in the Start With An Existing Form panel. Ticking it makes the Target Form name abbr field appear.
Target Form name abbr
The new Feature ID for a duplicated form. It cannot conflict with the Feature ID of the older form.
List Forms
The button that opens the Forms List for the selected tenant and OOU Code.
Forms List
The window listing the available forms, with a Search forms box and an arrow on each row for selecting the form to replicate.
Report Type
The type of form being created. In the Reports group it is always set to Custom, because custom forms are the ones configured. In the App Definition group it is a dropdown (RawData, Aggregate, SummativeAssessment, Kasa) in which RawData is selected.
Feature Type
A dropdown in the App Definition group with the options Custom, MultipleResponse and Standard. Custom is the type generally created; MultipleResponse is chosen when multiple responses are submitted for the form.
Actor Details
The actors who will fill up the form.
Workflow Details
The workflow of the form, set according to the requirement: which actor fills the form, which signs or reviews it, and which has view access only.
Auto Notification Details
The notifications that are active in the particular form.
Initiated By
A dropdown (Delegate, Student, Admin) used to select who fills up the form first, that is, who starts the form.
autoReminder
An option that must always be kept off. It is ticked by default on a new form and is unticked on every form.
Sections tab (Layout Summary)
The tab where the questions of a form are organised. Its area is called the Layout Summary.
Section
A group created by typing a name in Caption and clicking Add Section. Fields (questions) are added to a section.
Caption
The field in which the name of a new section is typed.
Add Field
The button on a section that opens the field box, which has Main and Advanced sub-tabs.
Description
In the field box, the question that needs to be added.
Meta Information
The sub-information related to the particular question.
Control type
A dropdown that sets the kind of field used for the question. Control types are covered separately.
Property Name
A required entry on the Advanced sub-tab that identifies a question. It must be unique for each and every question.
fieldId
An identifier shown on the Advanced sub-tab. In the example it is the Feature ID of the form followed by the Property Name.
Validation (required)
A rule added with Add Validation. Choosing required makes the question mandatory, and a Message is then chosen to suit the question.
instanceForm
A checkbox on the Form tab, unticked by default. It is ticked when an instance-based form is being created.
Instance-based form
A form configured with instances according to the actors who fill it up, for example Student and Instructor.
Instance Id
The required name of an instance in the Instances list on the Form tab. One instance is added for each actor who fills up the form.
Layout tab
The tab where the layout is prepared so that steps can be added to the workflow.
Summary
An entry on the Layout tab, added with Summary Id and Add Summary. The first summary is added at first, to start adding instance fields.
Edit (summary sections)
A checkbox on each section row in a summary. It sets whether the section is editable on the actor's side. Ticked means editable, unticked means not editable.
Fields (summary sub-tab)
A sub-tab of a summary used to add any field that needs to be excluded from, or shown to, the actor.
FieldsInstances (summary sub-tab)
A sub-tab of a summary where the main part of the instance setup takes place. It starts with "No Instances are added" and an Add Instances button.
Workflow tab
The tab where the steps of the workflow are listed and set up, using the layout prepared on the Layout tab.
MultipleResponse (Feature Type)
The Feature Type chosen when multiple responses will be submitted for the form.
isMultiResponse
An option in App Definition that is ticked for a multi response form. It is unticked by default.
datepicker
A control type used for a date question, such as Date of Initiation.
Label, Short label, Name, Detail
Fields in the App Definition group that are filled automatically with the name of the form when a new form is created.
Version suffix (Ver.MM.YYYY)
The text appended to the end of the form name when a new version of an existing form is created, giving the version month and year. For example: Student Evaluation of Preceptor Ver.08.2026. No "New" prefix or suffix is used.
Replicate
To make a copy of an existing form, which then opens in the editor.
Editor tabs
The tabs across the top of the editor: Form, Sections, Layout, Workflow, Notification and Terms.
